chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah ibn Sadah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'Allah does not hold you accountable for oaths that are unintentional' (1). He said: 'Unintentional (al-laghw) is when a man says 'No, by Allah' or 'Yes, by Allah' without intending to bind himself to anything.'

key_terms.يَعْقِدُ: To bind or commit (in a legal sense)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'al-laghw' in oaths according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'al-laghw' refers to casual exclamations like 'by Allah' used for emphasis rather than binding legal oaths (yamin), distinguishing them from intentional vows. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining when an oath incurs expiation (kaffarah) versus when it is merely a figure of speech. The hadith underscores the importance of intention (niyyah) in the validity of oaths, a key principle in Usul al-Fiqh.
